rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> two-season (2007<U+2013>08, 2008<U+2013>09) field experiment at BARI Gazipur with nine drip-irrigation-level <U+00D7> mulch treatments in RCBD, three replications; own yield, water use, WUE (Figure 1) and economic data reported.
rows.notes: The study does report the figure the passage cites: WUE of 592 kg/ha/mm (<U+2248>59.2 kg/m3) for drip at 50% ETc under black polyethylene mulch (Water use and WUE section, Figure 1). However, every treatment in the trial is drip-irrigated; the factors varied are irrigation level (100/75/50% ETc) and mulch type (none/polyethylene/straw). There is no comparison with a non-drip method, so the study's own result is evidence about deficit irrigation and mulching under drip, not about drip irrigation delivering water conservation or higher water productivity relative to other methods. Per the instructions (a mulch trial under drip is evidence about mulch, not drip), Q2 is answered no. Single site, one soil, one crop and cultivar; only CV and LSD given, no SD/CI for WUE; no stated limitations. If a rater treats the passage as a mere restatement of the reported WUE value, Q2 could be yes with Q3<U+2013>Q9 no.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). All treatments are drip-fed from gravity tanks; the trial isolates irrigation amount and mulch effects, not drip versus other irrigation methods.
